title: Private VPC onboarding handbook: minimal-egress canary, operator-locked upgrade escape-hatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Author an onboarding handbook and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC customers that defines a zero/limited-egress canary path, a documented operator-locked upgrade escape-hatch, and minimal telemetry requirements for safe upgrades in air-gapped or highly restricted networks.
background: Customers deploying Redwood Private in heavily restricted VPCs frequently request: deterministic upgrade behavior with zero unexpected egress, a lightweight canary test that runs without external internet, a documented operator unlock/escape procedure when upgrades deadlock, and guarantees around telemetry and artifact provenance. Existing PRDs cover offline upgrades and mirrors but do not provide a single, prescriptive onboarding checklist or an operator-locked emergency flow for regionally isolated customers.
goals: Produce a single onboarding handbook for Private/VPC installations focused on networking and upgrade safety
Define a zero/egress-minimal canary validation suite that runs from an isolated mirror
Specify an operator-locked mode and stepwise escape-hatch with playbooks and API endpoints for controlled rollback/unlock
Capture acceptance criteria that QA and solutions engineering can run during customer onboarding
Ensure telemetry and audit logging meet privacy constraints while providing upgrade observability
scope_in: Network contracts: MTU, DNS split-horizon guidance, required allowlist for optional mirrors
Canary test suite that validates pod scheduling, image signature verification, KMS key access mock, and operator health without external egress
Operator-locked upgrade state machine and documented escape-hatch commands with gated approvals
Acceptance criteria for image provenance, checksum validation, and artifact mirror sync checks
Minimal telemetry spec (aggregated heartbeats, encrypted status, no payload) and retention guidance
scope_out: Implementation code changes to the operator (this ticket is PRD/acceptance only)
Automated mirror infrastructure build-out (covered in infra project tickets)
Commercial contract or legal terms changes
acceptance_criteria: Onboarding handbook exists in docs with step-by-step 'Network Readiness' checklist and example iptables/route rules for common enterprise topologies
Canary suite can be executed from an isolated mirror node and returns a pass/fail report without attempting internet egress
Upgrade can be paused and resumed via documented operator-locked commands; pausing leaves cluster in a known, recoverable state
Escape-hatch documented: operator-unlock command sequence, artifact fallback toggle, and image pinning procedure verified against a test cluster
Image and artifact signatures are validated by the canary and produce explicit error messages on mismatch
KMS rotation mock tests included and acceptance states for 'KMS unreachable' scenario described with rollback requirements
Telemetry emitted during canary is limited to heartbeats, component status, and compact metrics; no request/response payloads or customer prompt hashes
Audit log entries are emitted for every upgrade lifecycle step (start, canary pass/fail, pause, resume, unlock, rollback) with timestamps and operator identity
Operator and upgrade playbooks include SRE contact escalation, estimated time-to-recover, and a public rollback SLA for onboarding runs
validation_steps: 1) Run 'network-readiness' checklist in a staging VPC configured with zero outbound egress; capture pass/fail and attach logs
2) Execute canary from a local mirror (no internet) and verify artifacts are read from mirror and signatures verified
3) Trigger a simulated failed upgrade during canary; issue operator-lock and confirm cluster remains responsive for inference and control-plane operations
4) Perform unlock/escape-hatch steps against the simulated failure and validate the cluster returns to pre-upgrade state or successful rollback
5) Confirm telemetry output conforms to minimal schema and observe audit log entries for each lifecycle event
6) Run KMS-unreachable scenario and confirm fallback behavior and documented operator commands succeed
risks_mitigations: Risk: Customers misconfigure mirror and assume online access. Mitigation: pre-onboarding network test and sample iptables/route templates.
Risk: Operator-locked state may cause panic. Mitigation: include a clear, minimally privileged escape-hatch and require two-step approver confirmation in playbook.
Risk: Telemetry constraints prevent diagnosing failures. Mitigation: define minimal, reversible telemetry that preserves privacy while allowing root-cause indicators.
Risk: Image signature mismatch during canary. Mitigation: include artifact provenance troubleshooting steps and a temporary 'use-signed-cache' toggle for emergency recovery.
qa_test_cases: TC-ONB-001: Network readiness checklist run with zero egress - expected PASS for internal connectivity and mirror read
TC-CAN-002: Canary image verification - expected PASS when signatures match, explicit FAIL with remediation links when mismatch
TC-UPG-003: Pause during upgrade - expected cluster responsiveness maintained and all pods in stable state
TC-EH-004: Escape-hatch unlock - expected successful unlock and documented rollback completes without manual image re-fetch
notes: We should coordinate a dry run with Solutions Engineering and one pilot customer with an isolated VPC during the next cycle.
This handbook will be a prerequisite for issuing operator 'upgrade approvals' for air-gapped customers.
Include a short script bundle for customers to validate NTP, MTU, and DNS behavior prior to scheduling an onboarding run.
